cases.prompt: Explain why an HTTP client can receive a 304 response without a response body.
assertions: Lead with the reason for the missing body.
Keep HTTP terminology exact.
Preserve the causal stages in compact, natural prose.
Do not turn the answer into a generic documentation template or a telegraphic fragment.

cases.prompt: Rewrite: The retry can succeed, but it might return the same error and will not restore deleted data.
assertions: Preserve can, might, and will not as distinct levels of certainty.
Preserve the deletion caveat.
Do not add a guarantee.

cases.prompt: Turn these notes into a procedure: open Settings, choose API access, run tool auth --project acme-test, then confirm Status says Connected.
assertions: Use ordered steps.
Keep the command exact and format it as code.
Identify visible UI labels without relying on position.
Place verification after the action that produces it.

cases.prompt: Document createSession(userId, ttlSeconds), which returns a Session and can raise InvalidUser.
assertions: Preserve identifiers exactly.
Describe the method with a third-person present-tense verb.
Explain parameters, return information, and the error condition without inventing behavior.

cases.prompt: Review this notice, but do not rewrite it: Our revolutionary engine always guarantees instant results for every workload.
assertions: Report unsupported absolutes as the highest-impact problem.
Separate findings from optional improvements.
Do not replace the full notice.

cases.prompt: Po polsku wyjaśnij, czym różni się uwierzytelnianie od autoryzacji.
assertions: Respond in Polish.
Lead with the distinction.
Apply clarity principles without forcing English grammar conventions.

cases.prompt: Explain how to run DROP TABLE audit_events safely when the deletion cannot be reversed.
assertions: State the irreversible consequence explicitly.
Put prerequisites and verification before the destructive command.
Keep the SQL exact and do not compress the warning.

cases.prompt: Rewrite a setup page that uses 'click here', a bare URL, and an architecture image with no alt text.
assertions: Use descriptive link text.
Provide useful alt text when the image conveys information.
Do not rely on the image alone for required instructions.

cases.prompt: Light-edit a Markdown page without changing its heading IDs, code fences, or custom HTML attributes.
assertions: Preserve source constructs that affect rendering or links.
Make only changes required for clarity.
Do not convert formats without a destination requirement.

cases.prompt: Check whether sign in, signin, or sign-in is correct in a button label and in a noun phrase.
assertions: Distinguish grammatical roles instead of choosing one spelling globally.
Use the live word list when browsing is available.
Preserve an exact product label when the task does not permit changing it.

cases.prompt: An experienced engineer asks where the request timeout is configured. The only known fact is that server.timeout is assigned in src/server.js:42. Answer the question.
assertions: Answer with the exact symbol and location in one sentence or a short list.
Do not add headings, generic timeout background, troubleshooting steps, or speculation.
Keep server.timeout and src/server.js:42 exact.

cases.prompt: Write a short validation procedure. Node.js 18 is required. Run tool check --project acme and verify that it exits with status 0.
assertions: Keep the Node.js 18 prerequisite before the action.
Preserve tool check --project acme exactly.
Put the status 0 verification after the command.
Do not add an introduction, recap, optional commands, or unrelated setup.

cases.prompt: An engineer noticed that the deployment gate rejects a release when any required health check fails. Explain the behavior using only that fact.
assertions: State the gate rule and consequence directly.
Do not praise the engineer's observation or call it meaningful, insightful, important, or subtle.
Do not add a rhetorical setup, decorative metaphor, or unsupported rationale.

cases.prompt: Rewrite: It is important to note that the authentication layer is the connective tissue of the system. This is not merely configuration; it is a foundational contract. You have uncovered a meaningful edge case.
assertions: Preserve that authentication configuration is a shared system contract and that the edge case affects it.
Remove the importance announcement, decorative metaphor, canned contrast, and praise.
Use compact, natural, complete sentences rather than telegraphic fragments.

cases.prompt: The source says that automatic ETag generation defaults to weak in lib/application.js and compileETag in lib/utils.js compiles the setting. State the default and compilation point for an experienced contributor.
assertions: Answer in one to three sentences.
Keep lib/application.js, compileETag, and lib/utils.js exact.
Do not add response-generation, freshness, conditional-request, caching, testing, or troubleshooting details.

cases.prompt: You have finished checking the source. Answer the user: server.timeout is assigned in src/server.js:42. Where is the request timeout configured?
assertions: Return only the final answer.
Do not say that you will check, are checking, found the answer, or now have enough information.
Keep server.timeout and src/server.js:42 exact.

cases.prompt: Write the required local validation steps from these source facts: Node.js 18 is required; install with npm install; package.json defines npm run lint and npm test. Include no optional, adapted, or coverage commands.
assertions: Put Node.js 18 and npm install before validation.
Include npm run lint and npm test exactly.
Do not derive an npx command or add a CI, coverage, focused-test, or alternative command.

cases.prompt: A repository snapshot shows req.fresh calling fresh(req.headers, responseHeaders), but the fresh package source and documentation are absent. Explain the evidence boundary.
assertions: State what the repository proves about the call and delegation.
Do not invent how the fresh package parses or compares headers.
Identify the missing dependency evidence directly and stop.

cases.prompt: Explain this conditional response behavior: the framework generates an ETag when none exists, but a matching manually set ETag can also make the request fresh and produce 304.
assertions: Preserve both generated and manually set ETag paths.
Do not say that the absence of an existing ETag is required for every 304 response.
Use must, only, all, always, or never only if the stated evidence supports the quantifier.

cases.prompt: Draft a release note entry from these facts: version 2.4.0 shipped on 2026-08-12; the export job now retries up to 3 times; a request can time out after 30 seconds; the change fixed issue #418.
assertions: Keep 2.4.0, 3, 30 seconds, and #418 exact and use numerals for technical quantities.
Write the date as August 12, 2026 in prose or 2026-08-12 in a numeric field, never as a slash date.
Lead with the reader-facing change and its effect; keep the date because release notes are inherently time-stamped.
Do not add benefits, performance claims, or future promises that the facts don't support.

cases.prompt: Full-edit a setup page whose single wall of text mixes prerequisites, three ordered installation commands, a comparison of two deployment options, and a note that contains the required API key step.
assertions: Move the prerequisites and the required API key step out of the note and before the steps.
Use a numbered list for the ordered commands and a table only for the genuinely two-dimensional deployment comparison.
Use sentence-case, task-based headings with content after every heading.
Preserve every command and condition while restructuring.

cases.prompt: TLGD Explain in one or two sentences why a Git rebase changes commit hashes.
assertions: Answer directly in one or two sentences.
Do not echo TLGD, name the skill, or describe the style rules that were applied.
Keep Git terminology exact and do not add rebase workflow advice.
